column2: On the authority of Abū Hurayrah (may Allah the Exalted be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (Allah bless him and his family and grant them peace) said:

“Allah the Exalted is pure (ṭayyib) and accepts only what is pure. Allah has commanded the believers with what He commanded the messengers, for the Exalted said: ‘O messengers, eat of the good things and do righteous deeds’ [al-Muʾminūn 23:51], and the Exalted said:

‘O you who believe, eat of the good things We have provided you’ [al-Baqarah 2:172].” Then he mentioned a man who travels far, dishevelled and covered in dust, stretching his hands towards the sky: “O Lord! O Lord!”—“while his food is unlawful, his drink is unlawful, his clothing is unlawful and he has been nourished with the unlawful; so how can he be answered?” Reported by Muslim.
Ṭayyib (“pure”): holy, free of deficiencies and faults.
Lā yaqbalu (“does not accept”): of deeds and wealth,
Illā ṭayyiban (“except what is pure”): of deeds, that which is free of showing off, self-admiration and other things that spoil them; and of wealth, that which is purely lawful.
“With what He commanded the messengers”: eating of the good things and doing righteous deeds.
Ashʿath (“dishevelled”): with tangled hair.
Aghbar (“covered in dust”): dust-coloured from the length of his travel in acts of obedience.
“Stretching his hands”: raising them in supplication to Allah the Exalted.
Ghudhiya (“he has been nourished”): with ḍammah on the dotted ghayn and a light dhāl carrying kasrah.
“So how can he be answered?”: from where could one with these qualities be answered?
What is meant is that he is not fit to be answered; it is not an explicit statement that it is altogether impossible.
The command to make deeds sincerely for Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.
Encouragement to spend from what is lawful,
and the prohibition of spending from anything else.
The basic principle is that the prophets are equal to their nations in the rulings of the Sharīʿah, except where a proof establishes that something is specific to them.
Indulging in the unlawful prevents the acceptance of deeds and the answering of supplication.
Among the causes of supplication being answered are four things. The first is travelling far, because of the humility it brings, which is one of the greatest causes of an answer.

The second is a shabby appearance; that is why the Prophet ﷺ said: “Many a dishevelled, dusty person in two worn garments, turned away from doors, if he were to swear by Allah, Allah would fulfil it.”
The third is stretching the hands towards the sky, for Allah is Modest and Generous; He is too modest, when a man raises his hands to Him, to send them back empty and disappointed.
The fourth is persisting with Allah by repeatedly mentioning His lordship, which is among the greatest means by which an answer to supplication is sought.
